_comment: Re-derived 2026-10-17 from baseline run bench/load/baseline-runs/20261017T220243Z (current binary md5 4245c25446c9cecc4a2bed6defa52b75, .227 runner, homogeneous CPU pinning LOAD_ARM_CLASS=homogeneous ocserve=[0,4] freeze=[1,5] k6=[2,6], ROUNDS=2 requested / 1 complete interleaved pair delivered (round 2 aborted by the harness's fail-fast: the freeze control arm died under co-tenant memory pressure — MemAvailable hit 0.1 GB with two resident llama-servers), ladder 50,75,150, 0 errors on the ocserve cells). Formula (README): p95_ms_max = max(2 x baseline_worst_cell, baseline_worst_cell + 30). ocserve worst cell = 43.052ms (spread) -> max(86.1, 73.05) = 87; freeze worst cell = 581.365ms (spread) -> max(1162.73, 611.37) = 1163. err_rate_max = 0.005 (declared; both arms 0.000 on the closed cells). GATED invocation = this same closed config; the open-model arrival acceptance (A/B criteria in PERF-10X §1) is judged from the pre-registered arrival attempts, not this tripwire. Arrival separation is mechanical: GATED arrival runs get LOAD_ARRIVAL_GATE=1 (dropped==0 + err rate in-k6) via arrival_thresholds_env, never LOAD_P95_MAX. V2-mix runs (LOAD_INCLUDE_V2=1) are gated separately — never folded into this pool. Committed BEFORE any GATED=1 run. HONEST CAVEAT: the prior 2026-10-07 thresholds (65/1417) derived from a 4-thread pinning layout; this run used homogeneous 2-core-per-arm pinning and the current binary, so the numbers moved (ocserve 87 vs 65 reflects a different pinning class, not a regression: the current binary's recorded round-1 worst cell is 43ms, well inside the pre-fix 32ms envelope's order).
